recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. No FHIR-47275 source follow-up is needed in core; related applied issues such as FHIR-47619 and FHIR-48402 can be audited independently if desired.
issue_request: FHIR-47275 was Applied as Persuasive with Modification for R6 by Imaging Integration. It asked to clarify overlap between ImagingStudy and ImagingSelection, remove the implication that ImagingStudy may represent arbitrary subsets of a DICOM Study, update boundary text on both resource pages, and treat series/instance descriptions as known study content rather than clinical selections.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git commit 41a56bc14a79c48331002fc4e745c744208335d5, linked from Jira via HL7/fhir#3221, which updated the ImagingStudy and ImagingSelection introduction/boundary source. Later related description commits for FHIR-47662, FHIR-47664, and FHIR-47674 supplied the current known-count and Series/SOP Instance wording in the ImagingStudy StructureDefinition.
additional_context: Both resources are active in source/fhir.ini. September 2024 Imaging Integration minutes record the same FHIR-47275 scope, element-description, boundary, and use-case actions and split the use-case concern into FHIR-48402. FHIR-47619 is the same boundaries family and resolves by reference to FHIR-47275; later FHIR-54814 refined the boundary paragraph by adding the ImagingSelection.derivedFrom relationship.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current ImagingStudy prose says one ImagingStudy references one DICOM Study, can change as study information is added, and stores details of an entire DICOM Study; current ImagingSelection prose says it references a subset of a DICOM Study for a specific clinical purpose and is unlikely to change once created. Searches found no remaining stale subset-permission wording in the active ImagingStudy/ImagingSelection XML source.
